extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (computer algebra system) and its Normaliz/pointid/primdec libraries (mathematicians and computational-algebra practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular libraries (normaliz.lib, pointid.lib, primdec.lib) describing usage, return values, assumptions, options, and examples for computing invariants, monomial/valuation-based algebras, vanishing ideals of points, and primary decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectionValRings
rubrics_metrics.description: intersectionValRings(intmat V, intvec grading); Return: The function returns a monomial ideal, to be considered as the list of monomials generating S as an algebra over the coefficient field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: computes the subalgebra S = {f ∈ R : vi(f) ≥ 0, i = 1,...,r} for several discrete monomial valuations determined by the rows of V = (vi(Xj)). The function returns the ideal given by the input matrix V if one of the options supp, triang, volume, or hseries has been activated; in that case numerical invariants may be computed and other data written to files (see showNuminvs/exportNuminvs). Example usage and sample output provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectionValRingIdeals
rubrics_metrics.description: intersectionValRingIdeals(intmat V); intersectionValRingIdeals(intmat V, intvec grading); Return: The function returns two ideals, both to be considered as lists of monomials. The first is the system of monomial generators of S, the second the system of generators of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: computes S = {f ∈ R : vi(f) ≥ 0} for valuations vi and the S-submodule M = {f ∈ R : vi(f) ≥ wi} when wi (integers) are provided as the (n+1)-th column of V. Notes: gives an error if V has wrong number of columns. If options supp, triang, or hvect are activated the function returns the ideal given by input matrix T and may compute numerical invariants and write auxiliary files (see showNuminvs/exportNuminvs). Example usage and sample outputs provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: showNuminvs
rubrics_metrics.description: showNuminvs(); Purpose: prints the numerical invariants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printed invariants such as hilbert_basis_elements, number_extreme_rays, dim_max_subspace, embedding_dim, rank, external_index, internal_index, number_support_hyperplanes, size_triangulation, sum_dets, integrally_closed, inhomogeneous, graded, degree_1_elements, grading, grading_denom, multiplicity, multiplicity_denom, hilbert_series_num/denom, primary, class_group. See exportNuminvs to create top-level variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: exportNuminvs
rubrics_metrics.description: exportNuminvs(); Create: (creates top-level variables which contain the numerical invariants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on Normaliz options, different invariants are calculated. Use showNuminvs to see which invariants are available. Example: after exportNuminvs, variables like nmz_hilbert_basis_elements, nmz_number_extreme_rays, nmz_rank, nmz_number_support_hyperplanes, nmz_multiplicity, nmz_primary are set to numeric values.

rubrics_metrics.name: setNmzOption
rubrics_metrics.description: setNmzOption(string s, int onoff); Purpose: If onoff=1 the option s is activated, and if onoff=0 it is deactivated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Normaliz options are accessible via names: -s: supp, -t: triang, -v: volume, -p: hvect, -1: height1, -n: normal, -N: normal_l, -h: hilb, -d: dual, -a: allf, -c: control, -e: errorcheck, -B: bigint (Use GMP), -x=N: threads (set number of threads N; 0 means no explicit limiting). Note: in next version options will be accessible by Normaliz 3.0 names. Example shows setNmzOption("hilb",1) and showNmzOptions output.

rubrics_metrics.name: showNmzOptions
rubrics_metrics.description: showNmzOptions(); Return: Returns the string of activated options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This string is used as parameter when calling Normaliz. Example: after setNmzOption("hilb",1) showNmzOptions() returns '-f -h'.

rubrics_metrics.name: normaliz
rubrics_metrics.description: normaliz(intmat sgr, int nmz_mode); normaliz(intmat sgr, int nmz_mode, intmat sgr2, int nmz_mode2, ...); Return: The function applies Normaliz to the parameter sgr in the mode set by nmz_mode and returns the intmat defined by the file with suffix gen. Multiple (matrix,mode) pairs allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this version use old numerical types for input matrices: 0: cone, 1: cone_and_lattice, 2: polytope, 3: rees_algebra, 4: inequalities, 5: equations, 6: congruences, 10: lattice_ideal, 20: grading. Next version will expose Normaliz 3.0 names. Note: many higher-level procedures wrap Normaliz so calling this directly may not be necessary. Examples demonstrate calling with matrices and multiple modes; sample outputs shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: setNmzExecPath
rubrics_metrics.description: setNmzExecPath(string s); s path to the Normaliz executable. Create: Normaliz::nmz_exec_path to save the given path s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: not necessary if Normaliz executable is in system search path. Example: setNmzExecPath("../Normaliz/"). See setNmzOption/showNmzOptions for related configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: writeNmzData
rubrics_metrics.description: writeNmzData(intmat M, int mode); writeNmzData(intmat M, int mode, intmat M2, int mode2, ...); Purpose: Creates an input file for Normaliz from matrix M; second parameter sets the mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How matrix is interpreted depends on mode (see Normaliz documentation). Multiple (matrix,mode) pairs can be combined (useful to combine modes 4,5,6); use mode=20 to specify a grading. Needs an explicit filename set by setNmzFilename; filename is created from current filename. Note: most functions in normaliz.lib write/read data automatically so writeNmzData is rarely used explicitly. Examples show setNmzFilename and then writing files; sample content printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: readNmzData
rubrics_metrics.description: readNmzData(string suffix); Reads an output file of Normaliz containing an integer matrix and returns it as an intmat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filename is created from current filename and given suffix. Needs explicit filename set by setNmzFilename. Note: normaliz.lib functions usually read/write automatically so this is seldom used. This function reads only the first matrix in a file. Example shows setNmzFilename, using normaliz, then readNmzData("cst") returning matrix rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: setNmzFilename
rubrics_metrics.description: setNmzFilename(string s); Create: Normaliz::nmz_filename to save the given filename s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets filename for exchange of data; unless a path is set by setNmzDataPath, files are created in current directory. If a non-empty filename is set, files created for/by Normaliz are kept (mandatory for data access functions writeNmzData/readNmzData). Resetting to "" forces library to return to deletion of temporary files, but files created earlier remain. Example shows setNmzDataPath and setNmzFilename usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: setNmzDataPath
rubrics_metrics.description: setNmzDataPath(string s); Create: Normaliz::nmz_data_path to save the given path s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets path for exchange of data; default is current directory. Singular cannot use filenames starting with ~ or $HOME in its I/O; avoid path names starting with / under Cygwin since Singular and Normaliz interpret them differently. Example shows setNmzDataPath and setNmzFilename to place files in examples/.

rubrics_metrics.name: writeNmzPaths
rubrics_metrics.description: writeNmzPaths; Create: writes files nmz_sing_exec.path and nmz_sing_data.path saving exec path and data path respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If names not defined the corresponding file is created but empty. Files are saved in current directory. Example: setNmzExecPath("../Normaliz/"); writeNmzPaths(); reading nmz_sing_exec.path returns the path, data.path may be empty. See setNmzDataPath/setNmzExecPath/startNmz.

rubrics_metrics.name: startNmz
rubrics_metrics.description: startNmz(); Purpose: reads files written by writeNmzPaths(), retrieves path names and prints them to standard output (as far as set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a simple way to open a Normaliz session after path names have been stored. Example output shows nmz_exec_path and whether nmz_data_path is set. See related configuration functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: rmNmzFiles
rubrics_metrics.description: rmNmzFiles(); Purpose: removes the files created for and by Normaliz, using the last filename specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Needs an explicit filename set by setNmzFilename. Example: setNmzFilename("VeryInteresting"); rmNmzFiles(). See readNmzData/setNmzDataPath/writeNmzData for related I/O handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: mons2intmat
rubrics_metrics.description: mons2intmat(ideal I); Return: Returns the intmat whose rows represent the leading exponents of the (non-zero) elements of I. The length of each row is nvars(basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows conversion of monomial ideal to integer matrix of exponent vectors. See intmat2mons for inverse operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat2mons
rubrics_metrics.description: intmat2mons(intmat M); Return: an ideal generated by the monomials which correspond to the exponent vectors given by the rows of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precondition: number of variables in basering nvars(basering) must be at least ncols(M), otherwise the function exits with an error (see ERROR section). Example demonstrates conversion of exponent matrix back to monomials. See mons2intmat.

rubrics_metrics.name: binomials2intmat
rubrics_metrics.description: binomials2intmat(ideal I); Returns the intmat whose rows represent the exponents of the (non-zero) elements of I which have to be binomials. The length of each row is nvars(basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: for ideal of binomials ux2-xyz, ux2-vyz, uvw-y2z returns rows with positive/negative exponents reflecting binomials. See intmat2mons/mons2intmat.

rubrics_metrics.name: pointid library overview
rubrics_metrics.description: pointid.lib — Procedures for computing a factorized lex Gröbner basis of the vanishing ideal of a set of points via the Axis-of-Evil Theorem (M.G. Marinari, T. Mora).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview explains algorithm of Cerlienco-Mureddu associates to ordered set of points A in K^n a set of monomials N and bijection phi: A → N; N is monomial basis of K[x(1..n)]/I(A). Allows deducing corner-monomials M and a unique reduced lex Groebner basis G such that LM(fi)=mi. Also mentions canonical linear factorization of each Groebner basis element per Axis-of-Evil Theorem. Provides combinatorial algorithm and interpolation to produce y_mdi factors and factorizations fi = (product of y_mdi) modulo previous fi's. Procedures listed below implement these computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nonMonomials
rubrics_metrics.description: nonMonomials(id); id = <list of vectors> or <list of lists> or <module> or <matrix>. Return: ideal, the non-monomials of the vanishing ideal I(A) of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering has ordering rp (0,x(1..n),rp). Purpose: compute Mon(x(1),...,x(n)) \ {LM(f)| f in I(A)} using algorithm of Cerlienco-Mureddu. A (set of points) can be given as list of vectors/lists, a module (generators are points), or a matrix (columns are points). Examples show various input forms and produced non-monomials list.

rubrics_metrics.name: cornerMonomials
rubrics_metrics.description: cornerMonomials(N); N ideal. Return: ideal, the corner-monomials of the order ideal N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precondition: N must be an order ideal (if a monomial is in N then any of its factors is in N). The corner-monomials are the leading monomials of an ideal I such that N is a basis of basering/I. Note: in applications I is the vanishing ideal of a finite set of points. Example shows input basis N and output corner monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: facGBIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: facGBIdeal(id); id = <list of vectors> or <list of lists> or <module> or <matrix>. Return: a list where the first entry contains the Gröbner basis G of I(A) and the second entry contains the linear factors of each element of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering has ordering rp (0,x(1..n),rp). Combinatorial algorithm due to Axis-of-Evil Theorem (Marinari, Mora). The procedure returns both the reduced lex Gröbner basis for the vanishing ideal and a canonical linear factorization (list of linear factors) for each Groebner basis element. Examples demonstrate inputs as lists/matrices/modules and show both G and factor lists in output.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdec library overview
rubrics_metrics.description: primdec.lib — Primary Decomposition and Radical of Ideals. Overview: Algorithms for primary decomposition based on Gianni/Trager/Zacharias and Shimoyama/Yokoyama; procedures implemented to be used in characteristic 0 (work in large positive characteristic but primdecGTZ may not terminate in small characteristic). Radical algorithms based on Krick/Logar/Laplagne/Kemper; work in any characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baserings must have a global ordering and no quotient ideal for most procedures; exceptions (primdecGTZ, absPrimdecGTZ, minAssGTZ, primdecSY, minAssChar, radical) accept non-global ordering. Authors listed. Procedures implement primary decomposition, minimal associated primes, radicals, and related functionality; documented functions follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ann
rubrics_metrics.description: Ann(M); M module. Return: ideal, the annihilator of coker(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: output is the ideal of all elements a of the basering R such that a * R^m is contained in M (m = number of rows of M). Examples demonstrate usage on modules and behavior under qring mapping (imap).

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecGTZ
rubrics_metrics.description: primdecGTZ(I); I ideal. Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes for a proper ideal I, otherwise pr = list(list(ideal(1), ideal(1))). pr[i][1] is i-th primary component and pr[i][2] is i-th prime component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: Gianni/Trager/Zacharias. Designed for characteristic 0, may work in char k>0 if it terminates (can loop in small characteristic). For local orderings, result considered in localization of polynomial ring, not power series ring. For local/mixed orderings, decomposition in corresponding global ring is returned if 'global' specified as second argument. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecGTZE
rubrics_metrics.description: primdecGTZE(I); I ideal. Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes for a proper ideal, and an empty list for the unit ideal. pr[i][1] is i-th primary component and pr[i][2] i-th prime component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same algorithmic notes as primdecGTZ: Gianni/Trager/Zacharias; designed for characteristic 0; for local orderings result considered in localization; 'global' string can request global decomposition. Example shows behavior and that unit ideal returns empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecSY
rubrics_metrics.description: primdecSY(I, c); I ideal, c int (optional). Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes for proper ideal I, otherwise pr[1] is list(ideal(1),ideal(1)). pr[i][1] is i-th primary component and pr[i][2] i-th prime component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: Shimoyama/Yokoyama. Parameter c controls ordering strategy: c=0 uses given variable ordering; c=1 minAssChar tries to use an optimal ordering (default); c=2 uses minAssGTZ; c=3 uses minAssGTZ and facstd. For local orderings result considered in localization; for local/mixed orderings, 'global' can be specified as third argument to get global decomposition. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecSYE
rubrics_metrics.description: primdecSYE(I, c); I ideal, c int (optional). Return: a list pr of primary ideals and their associated primes; if I is the unit ideal returns an empty list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: Shimoyama/Yokoyama. Same parameter behavior for c as primdecSY (c=0 given ordering; c=1 minAssChar; c=2 minAssGTZ; c=3 minAssGTZ+facstd). Local ordering behavior same as primdecSY. Examples show behavior including unit ideal returning empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssGTZ
rubrics_metrics.description: minAssGTZ(I[, l]); I ideal, l optional list of options. Return: a list, the minimal associated prime ideals of proper ideal I, otherwise ideal(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters in l: 0, 'facstd' uses facstd to first decompose (default); 1, 'noFacstd' disable that; 'GTZ' original algorithm; 'SL' GTZ algorithm with Laplagne modifications (default). Designed for characteristic 0, works in char k>0 based on Yokoyama algorithm. For local orderings result considered in localization; for local/mixed orderings, specify 'global' to get global decomposition. Example usage shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssGTZE
rubrics_metrics.description: minAssGTZE(I[, l]); I ideal, l optional list. Return: a list, the minimal associated prime ideals of I. Returns empty list for unit ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same optional parameters and algorithmic notes as minAssGTZ. Example provided and note that minAssGTZE(J) for J=1 returns empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: minAssChar
rubrics_metrics.description: minAssChar(I[,c]); I ideal, c int (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry begins the documentation for minAssChar (procedure for computing minimal associated primes tailored to characteristic considerations). The chunk provides the Usage header only; full behavior and notes are documented in continuation of the manual (not included in this chunk).
